mainTopic: The power of the יצר הרע, the seriousness of sinful intention, and the laws of יחוד with relatives and children
overview: The amud opens by finishing the story of פלימו, who used to taunt שטן. שטן embarrasses him and then teaches him to say instead, 'May the Merciful One rebuke שטן.' Next comes the story of the elderly רבי חייא בר אשי. He gives in to his wife, who is disguised as a prostitute, and then fasts for the rest of his life because he meant to sin. A ברייתא about a woman whose נזיר vow was cancelled without her knowing shows that even a sinful intention needs forgiveness. This leads רבי עקיבא and איסי בן יהודה to cry over how serious sin is. The גמרא then returns to the משנה's rules of יחוד. רב אסי allows it with close relatives, but שמואל forbids it with all עריות, even an animal, and the גמרא concludes that this is a dispute among תנאים. רבא lists pairs of women a man may be alone with, and the גמרא sets the ages at which children may no longer share a bed with a parent. The amud ends with a story about רב אחא בר אבא holding his granddaughter, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: שטן provokes פלימו and fakes his own death
steps.stepSummary: The disguised שטן behaves disgustingly at פלימו's table, then pretends to die so that people blame פלימו for killing him.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Sit properly.' He said to him: 'Give me a cup.' They gave him a cup. He coughed up his phlegm and spat it into the cup. They scolded him. He sank down and died. They heard people saying: 'פלימו killed a man! פלימו killed a man!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of a story from the previous page. שטן, disguised as a poor guest, keeps making trouble at פלימו's house and then fakes his own death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פלימו used to taunt שטן by saying 'an arrow in שטן's eye.' Here שטן gets back at him. First he acts revoltingly, and then he 'dies' so that פלימו is suspected of murder.

keyTerms.meaning: The Satan, the force that tempts people and accuses them
He sank down and died (here, only pretending)

phrases.english: Sit properly.
He said to him: Give me a cup.
They gave him a cup.
He coughed up and spat his phlegm into it.
They scolded him.
He sank down and died.
phrases.notes: He didn't really die. שטן is only putting on a show.

phrases.english: They heard people saying:

phrases.aramaic: פְּלֵימוֹ קְטַל גַּבְרָא! פְּלֵימוֹ קְטַל גַּבְרָא!
phrases.english: Peleimu killed a man! Peleimu killed a man!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of פלימו from the previous page
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שטן punishes פלימו's taunting by making him look like a murderer

steps.title: פלימו hides and שטן reveals himself
steps.stepSummary: פלימו runs away in fear and hides. שטן follows him and, seeing how much he is suffering, reveals who he really is.
steps.simpleTranslation: He fled and hid himself in the bathroom. He followed him and fell before him. When he saw that he was suffering, he revealed himself to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. פלימו panics and hides, and שטן finally shows him who he really is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שטן keeps up the act even after פלימו runs away. He follows him and 'falls' in front of him. He stops only once פלימו is truly suffering, because by then the lesson has been driven home.

phrases.english: He fled and hid himself in the bathroom.
He followed him and fell before him.
phrases.notes: Here 'he' is שטן, still pretending, following פלימו into his hiding place.

phrases.english: When he saw that he was suffering,
he revealed himself to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story directly from step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שטן ends the deception once פלימו is suffering

steps.title: The proper way to speak about שטן
steps.stepSummary: שטן asks פלימו why he used to taunt him. פלימו asks what he should say instead, and שטן tells him to say: 'May the Merciful One rebuke שטן.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'Why did you speak this way?' 'But how else should I speak?' He said to him: 'Let the master say: May the Merciful One rebuke שטן.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the lesson of the פלימו story. Instead of taunting שטן yourself, ask ה׳ to rebuke him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'an arrow in שטן's eye' was a personal challenge, and it invited שטן to strike back. The better phrase does not pick a fight. It turns to the Merciful One to deal with שטן.
steps.whatToRemember: Don't challenge the יצר הרע or שטן through your own boldness. Ask ה׳ to rebuke him.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי טַעְמָא אָמְרַתְּ הָכִי?
phrases.english: He said to him: Why did you speak this way?
phrases.notes: 'This way' means פלימו's habit, from earlier in the story, of saying 'an arrow in שטן's eye.'

phrases.english: But how then should I say?
He said to him: Let the master say:
'May the Merciful One rebuke the Satan.'
phrases.notes: This sounds like the words in זכריה 3:2.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי טַעְמָא אָמְרַתְּ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the moral of the story once שטן has revealed himself
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The right response to שטן is 'May the Merciful One rebuke שטן,' not a personal taunt

steps.title: רבי חייא בר אשי's prayer puzzles his wife
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אשי always prays to be saved from the יצר הרע. His wife wonders why, since he has kept away from her for years.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אשי had a habit: whenever he fell on his face in prayer, he would say, 'May the Merciful One save us from the יצר הרע.' One day his wife heard him. She said: 'It has been several years since he separated from me. Why does he say this?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about how strong the יצר הרע is. This step sets it up by telling us about the prayer and the wife's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife thinks her elderly husband no longer has any desire, so his prayer seems pointless. Her question is what leads into the test in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Falling on his face (the תחנון prayer)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי הֲוָה רְגִיל
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Ashi was accustomed,
whenever he would fall on his face in prayer,
to say: 'May the Merciful One save us from the evil inclination.'
One day his wife heard him.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording, 'heard him.'

phrases.english: She said: After all, it has been several years
since he separated from me.
Why does he say this?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי הֲוָה רְגִיל כׇּל עִידָּן דַּהֲוָה נָפֵל לְאַפֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story on the same theme of the יצר הרע's power
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even an elderly צדיק prays daily to be saved from the יצר הרע

steps.title: The wife's disguise and his failure in the garden
steps.stepSummary: His wife dresses up as the prostitute חרותא. He propositions her and fetches the pomegranate she asks for as payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day he was learning in his garden. She adorned herself and kept passing in front of him. He said to her: 'Who are you?' She said: 'I am חרותא, coming back from my day.' He propositioned her. She said to him: 'Bring me that pomegranate at the top of the tree.' He leapt up, went, and brought it to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The wife puts her husband to the test, and he gives in to the יצר הרע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers the wife's question from step 4. Even in old age and in the middle of learning, his desire came right back. That shows his prayer was not pointless at all.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹמָא חֲדָא הֲוָה קָא גָרֵיס בְּגִינְּתֵיהּ.
phrases.english: One day he was studying in his garden.
She adorned herself and passed back and forth before him.
He said to her: Who are you?
She said: I am Ḥaruta, returning from my day.
phrases.notes: חרותא was the name of a well-known prostitute, so she is pretending to be her.

phrases.english: He propositioned her.
She said to him: Bring me
that pomegranate at the top of the tree.
He leapt up, went, and brought it to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹמָא חֲדָא הֲוָה קָא גָרֵיס בְּגִינְּתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wife's question by showing the test
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יצר הרע can overpower even an elderly צדיק

steps.title: He sits in the oven and his wife reveals the truth
steps.stepSummary: Overcome with guilt, he sits inside the burning oven. His wife tells him it was really her, but he believes her only after she gives him signs.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he came home, his wife was lighting the oven. He went up and sat inside it. She said to him: 'What is this?' He said to her: 'Such and such happened.' She said to him: 'It was me.' He paid no attention to her until she gave him signs.
steps.whatsHappening: The story reaches its turning point. He tries to punish himself, and his wife tells him what really happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sitting in the oven shows how deeply sorry he was. He doesn't believe his wife at first because he thinks she is only trying to comfort him. Only clear proof convinces him.

phrases.english: When he came home,
his wife was lighting the oven.
He went up and sat inside it.
She said to him: What is this?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לַהּ: הָכִי וְהָכִי הֲוָה מַעֲשֶׂה.
phrases.english: He said to her: Such and such an incident happened.
She said to him: It was I.
He paid no attention to her,
until she gave him signs.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא לְבֵיתֵיהּ הֲוָה קָא שָׁגְרָא דְּבֵיתְהוּ תַּנּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows what happened after the garden incident
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He punishes himself and learns that the woman was his own wife

steps.title: His intention still counted, so he fasted all his life
steps.stepSummary: Even though she was really his wife, he says that he meant to sin. He fasts for the rest of his life until he dies of that grief.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: 'I, at any rate, intended to do something forbidden.' All the days of that צדיק he fasted, until he died from it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the ending of the story. He refuses to excuse himself, because in his mind he chose to sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No sin happened in fact, since the woman was his wife. But he held himself responsible for what he meant to do. His lifelong fasting shows how seriously he took a sinful intention.

keyTerms.meaning: At any rate, in any case
I intended to do something forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: An elderly צדיק fell to the יצר הרע, so no one is too old or too holy to need protection. And even a sin that never actually happened can call for תשובה because of what the person meant to do.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think he actually sinned with a forbidden woman. She was his own wife. He grieved over his intention, not over the act itself.

phrases.english: He said to her: I, in any event,
intended to do something forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל יָמָיו שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ צַדִּיק הָיָה מִתְעַנֶּה
phrases.english: All the days of that righteous man, he would fast,
until he died by that death.
phrases.notes: He means he died from that same grief and fasting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story by showing his response to learning the truth
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Intending to sin is serious enough to call for תשובה, and the יצר הרע threatens even the greatest people

steps.title: A source: the woman who did not know her vow was cancelled
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that the פסוק‎ 'ה׳ will forgive her' is about a woman who broke her נזיר vow without knowing her husband had already cancelled it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'Her husband cancelled them, and ה׳ will forgive her.' What case is the פסוק talking about? A woman who vowed to be a נזיר. Her husband heard and cancelled the vow, but she did not know. So she went ahead and drank wine and became impure from the dead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as proof that a person who meant to sin needs forgiveness, even if no real sin happened. This backs up what רבי חייא בר אשי felt in the story we just finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman's vow was already cancelled, so the wine and the impurity were actually allowed. But she thought she was breaking her vow. The Torah still says she needs ה׳'s forgiveness, so the bad intention alone needs forgiveness.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who vows not to drink wine and not to become impure from the dead

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the Torah source behind the whole idea that a sinful plan, even one that never really happened, needs atonement.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
"Her husband has cancelled them, and ה׳ will forgive her"
phrases.notes: במדבר 30:13

phrases.english: What case is the verse talking about?
A woman who vowed to be a nazir,
and her husband heard and cancelled it for her,

phrases.aramaic: וְהִיא לֹא יָדְעָה שֶׁהֵפֵר לָהּ בַּעְלָהּ,
phrases.english: but she did not know that her husband had cancelled it,
and she was drinking wine
and becoming impure from the dead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the Torah source for רבי חייא בר אשי's feeling that he needed atonement for what he meant to do.
steps.raayaObject: That a person who meant to sin needs forgiveness even if he did not really sin.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on במדבר 30:13 about a woman whose נזיר vow was cancelled without her knowing.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא cries: if a mistaken sinner needs forgiveness, how much more a real one
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא would cry at this פסוק. He built a קל וחומר: if someone who meant to eat pork but ate lamb needs atonement, then someone who really ate pork needs it even more.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whenever רבי עקיבא reached this פסוק, he would cry. He said: Someone who meant to eat pork but actually got lamb still needs atonement and forgiveness, says the Torah. So someone who meant to eat pork and really got pork needs it so much more!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells how רבי עקיבא reacted to this פסוק. He uses it to show how serious a real sin must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman is like the person who wanted pork but got lamb: she meant to sin, but nothing forbidden happened. If even that needs forgiveness, a sin that was both planned and done is much worse. That thought is what made רבי עקיבא cry.

keyTerms.meaning: Came into his hand; what actually ended up happening
How much more so; the ending words of a קל וחומר

phrases.english: When Rabbi Akiva would reach
this verse, he would cry.
He said: Now if someone who intended
to eat pork
and lamb meat ended up in his hand,
the Torah says: She needs atonement and forgiveness,
then someone who intended to eat pork
and pork ended up in his hand,
how much more so!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא כִּי הֲוָה מָטֵי לְהַאי פְּסוּקָא הֲוָה בָּכֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a קל וחומר from the ברייתא's reading of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If meaning to sin without really sinning needs atonement, a sin that was both meant and done needs it much more.

steps.title: A second פסוק that made רבי עקיבא cry
steps.stepSummary: The same lesson comes from 'He did not know, yet he is guilty'. Someone who meant to eat permitted fat but ate forbidden fat is still guilty. So someone who meant to eat forbidden fat and did is guilty even more.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say the same about the פסוק 'He did not know, yet he is guilty and shall carry his sin.' When רבי עקיבא reached this פסוק he would cry. Someone who meant to eat permitted fat but got forbidden fat is called guilty by the Torah. So someone who meant to eat forbidden fat and got forbidden fat is guilty so much more!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second פסוק that teaches a similar lesson. רבי עקיבא cried over this one too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case runs the other way from the first one. Here the person meant well but ended up doing something forbidden, and the Torah still calls him guilty. If an honest mistake carries guilt, a sin done on purpose carries much more.

keyTerms.meaning: In a similar way, along the same lines

steps.confusionAlert: The two cases are opposites. In the pork case he meant to sin but did nothing wrong. In the fat case he meant no harm but did something forbidden. Both lead to the same 'how much more' conclusion.

phrases.english: In a similar way, you can say about
"He did not know, yet he is guilty, and he shall carry his sin."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:17

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁהָיָה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מַגִּיעַ לְפָסוּק זֶה
phrases.english: When Rabbi Akiva reached this verse
he would cry:
Now if someone who intended to eat permitted fat
and forbidden fat ended up in his hand,

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה תּוֹרָה: ״וְלֹא יָדַע וְאָשֵׁם וְנָשָׂא עֲוֹנוֹ״,
phrases.english: the Torah says: "He did not know, yet he is guilty, and he shall carry his sin,"
then someone who intended to eat forbidden fat
and forbidden fat ended up in his hand,
how much more so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel פסוק and a parallel קל וחומר from רבי עקיבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If doing something forbidden by mistake makes a person guilty, a planned sin makes him much more guilty.

steps.title: איסי בן יהודה: everyone should grieve over this
steps.stepSummary: איסי בן יהודה says that the פסוק 'He did not know, yet he is guilty' is something every grieving person should mourn over.
steps.simpleTranslation: איסי בן יהודה says about 'He did not know, yet he is guilty and shall carry his sin': over this, all who grieve should grieve.
steps.whatsHappening: Another תנא adds his own feeling about the same פסוק. It closes this short section about intention and guilt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איסי בן יהודה does not build a קל וחומר. He just says the פסוק itself is worth mourning over, because a person can be guilty even without knowing he sinned.
steps.whatToRemember: A sinful plan needs atonement even if no sin happened, and an honest mistake still carries guilt. That is why רבי עקיבא cried, and why איסי בן יהודה said everyone should grieve.

phrases.english: Isi ben Yehuda says:
"He did not know, yet he is guilty, and he shall carry his sin":

phrases.aramaic: עַל דָּבָר זֶה יִדְווּ כׇּל הַדּוֹוִים.
phrases.english: Over this matter, all who grieve should grieve.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another Tanna's emotional reaction to the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Being guilty without knowing it is something worth mourning over.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: being alone with close relatives
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that a man may be alone with his mother. רב אסי adds that he may also be alone with his sister, and may even live together with his mother and daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'A man may be alone with his mother.' רב יהודה said in the name of רב אסי: A man may be alone with his sister, and he may live in the same home as his mother and his daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the משנה about יחוד. רב אסי gives a broad היתר for close family members.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentions a mother and a daughter. רב אסי adds a sister for being alone together, and allows a mother and a daughter even to share a home long-term. This sets up שמואל's reaction in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Is alone together (the issue of יחוד)

phrases.english: "A man may be alone with his mother."
phrases.notes: These words are quoted from our משנה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav Asi:
A man may be alone with his sister,
and he may live with his mother and with his daughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story-based section and goes back to the משנה's rule on יחוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אסי: a man may be alone with his sister, and may live with his mother and his daughter.

steps.title: שמואל: no being alone with any forbidden relative, even an animal
steps.stepSummary: When רב יהודה repeated רב אסי's היתר in front of שמואל, שמואל said it is forbidden to be alone with any of the Torah's forbidden relations, and even with an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I said this in front of שמואל, he said: It is forbidden to be alone with any of the forbidden relations of the Torah, and even with an animal.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל rejects רב אסי's היתר. He says the rule of יחוד covers every Torah-forbidden relation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי allowed close family members. שמואל says no: every relation the Torah forbids is included, even a sister, mother, or daughter. He adds an animal to show how wide the rule is.

phrases.english: When I said it in front of Shmuel,
phrases.notes: With the letters in square brackets, this reads 'when I said it'. רב יהודה is telling what happened when he repeated רב אסי's words.

phrases.english: he said: It is forbidden to be alone
with any of the forbidden relations of the Torah,
and even with an animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: שמואל rejects רב אסי's היתר from the previous step.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב אסי's היתר to be alone with a sister and to live with a mother and a daughter.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rule of יחוד covers all עריות of the Torah, with no exception for close family, and even includes an animal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל: it is forbidden to be alone with any of the עריות of the Torah, including close relatives, and even with an animal.

steps.title: The משנה Seems to Refute שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings our משנה, which allows a man to be alone with his mother and daughter, as a refutation of שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: a man may be alone with his mother and with his daughter, and may even sleep next to them with bodily contact. This is a refutation of שמואל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's strict view from the previous step, using the words of our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said you may not be alone with any of the עריות. The משנה clearly allows being alone with a mother and daughter, and even sleeping close to them. A משנה outranks an אמורא, so this looks like a תיובתא, a decisive refutation.

phrases.english: We learned: A man may be alone with his mother
and with his daughter
and he may sleep with them with bodily contact,
and this is a refutation of Shmuel!
phrases.notes: שמואל is the one from the step before, who forbade being alone with any ערוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's ruling from step 13 using the משנה quoted in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that one may not be alone with any ערוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה explicitly allows being alone with a mother and daughter, which directly contradicts שמואל.

steps.title: שמואל Points to a ברייתא on His Side
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers with a ברייתא that allows being alone with any ערוה, including a sister or mother-in-law, only when witnesses are present.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל could answer you: By your reasoning, what will you do with the ברייתא that says a man may be alone with his sister, his mother-in-law, and all the other עריות in the תורה only when witnesses are present? With witnesses, yes. Without witnesses, no!
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל pushes back by showing that a ברייתא agrees with him. So the משנה is not the only source on this question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא includes "all the עריות in the תורה", so it covers a mother and daughter too. It allows יחוד only with witnesses. The questioner has to explain this ברייתא too, which shows the sources themselves disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your own reasoning
Relatives the תורה forbids for relations

phrases.english: Shmuel could say to you:
And according to your reasoning, what about that which is taught in a baraita:
His sister, and his mother-in-law,
and all the other forbidden relations in the Torah,
one may be alone with them only in the presence of witnesses.
With witnesses, yes;
without witnesses, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends שמואל by showing a ברייתא that contradicts the משנה used against him.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-source: showing the earlier sources disagree among themselves
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה settles the matter against שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: A ברייתא supports שמואל, so the question cannot be settled by the משנה alone.

steps.title: It Is a Dispute Among תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the משנה and the ברייתא reflect a dispute among תנאים, and שמואל follows one side.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a dispute among תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up: this question was argued about by the תנאים themselves. It is setting up the next step, which shows that dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the משנה allows it and the ברייתא forbids it, neither side refutes the other. שמואל is not refuted, he simply holds like the strict תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute among תנאים

phrases.english: Rather, it is a dispute between tanna'im.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the clash between the משנה and the ברייתא by calling it a dispute among תנאים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Making it a dispute among earlier authorities (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל is refuted by the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל follows the תנאים who forbid יחוד even with close relatives.

steps.title: רבי מאיר and רבי טרפון Were Careful Even with Close Relatives
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבי מאיר and רבי טרפון asking to be watched around a daughter and a daughter-in-law. A student who mocked this soon sinned with his own mother-in-law.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the ברייתא teaches: רבי מאיר said, "Watch me because of my daughter." רבי טרפון said, "Watch me because of my daughter-in-law." A certain student mocked him. רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי חנינא בן גמליאל: only a few days passed before that student stumbled into sin with his mother-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that shows the strict side of the dispute among תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Great תנאים worried about being alone even with a daughter or daughter-in-law, which matches שמואל's strict view. The story of the student warns that no one should feel too sure of himself in these matters.

keyTerms.meaning: Be careful with me, keep an eye on me

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the strict approach to יחוד has strong support among the תנאים, and that it guards against real danger.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Meir said:
Be careful with me because of my daughter.
phrases.notes: He means: make sure I'm never left alone with her.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon said:
Be careful with me because of my daughter-in-law.
A certain student mocked him.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said in the name of Rabbi Ḥanina ben Gamliel:
Only a few days passed
until that student stumbled into sin with his mother-in-law.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר: הִזָּהֲרוּ בִּי מִפְּנֵי בִּתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the ברייתא that shows the strict side of the dispute among תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: That some תנאים forbade יחוד even with close relatives, like שמואל
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא quoting רבי מאיר and רבי טרפון, plus the story of the student

steps.title: How אביי and רב ששת Kept Away from Animals
steps.stepSummary: Following שמואל's rule that even being alone with an animal is forbidden, אביי cleared animals from the whole field, and רב ששת moved them across the fence.
steps.simpleTranslation: About "even with an animal": אביי would remove the animals from the whole field. רב ששת would move them to the other side of the fence.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the last part of שמואל's statement, "even with an animal", and tells how אמוראים kept it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל included animals in the איסור of יחוד. These stories show that leading אמוראים really kept this, each in his own way.

phrases.english: Even with an animal:
phrases.notes: These are שמואל's words from step 13; the גמרא now picks them up.

phrases.english: Abaye would remove them
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is the corrected spelling of the word.

phrases.english: from the entire field.
Rav Sheshet would move them to the other side of the fence.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ עִם בְּהֵמָה אַבָּיֵי מְכַלֵּי לֵיהּ מִכּוּלֵּהּ דַּבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the second part of שמואל's statement, about animals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אמוראים actually kept the איסור of being alone with an animal.

steps.title: רב חנן Finds רב כהנא Alone with an Animal
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן from נהרדעא visits רב כהנא, sees an animal in front of him while he learns, and asks if he doesn't hold of the איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנן from נהרדעא came to visit רב כהנא in פום נהרא. He saw him sitting and learning, with an animal standing in front of him. He asked him: "Doesn't the master hold that even being alone with an animal is forbidden?"
steps.whatsHappening: A story sets up a question: why was רב כהנא alone with an animal? The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since אביי and רב ששת were so careful, רב כהנא's behavior looks strange. רב חנן wants to know if רב כהנא disagrees with שמואל's rule.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥanan from Neharde'a
happened to come to Rav Kahana in Pum Nahara.
He saw that he was sitting and learning,
and an animal was standing in front of him.
He said to him:
Does the master not hold
"even with an animal"?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר אֲפִילּוּ עִם בְּהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story that seems to go against the practice of אביי and רב ששת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב כהנא disagrees with the איסור of being alone with an animal

steps.title: רב כהנא Had Not Noticed the Animal
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that he did not notice the animal was there.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered him: "I didn't notice it."
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא explains that he does hold of the איסור, he just did not realize the animal was in front of him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His answer shows he does not argue with שמואל. It was simply a case of not paying attention while he was busy learning.

keyTerms.meaning: It was not on my mind, I didn't notice

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's איסור of being alone with an animal was accepted. רב כהנא did not argue with it, he simply had not noticed the animal.

phrases.english: He said to him: It was not on my mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חנן's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב כהנא holds of the איסור; he simply did not notice the animal.

steps.title: רבא's List of Women a Man May Be Alone With
steps.stepSummary: רבא allows a man to be alone with pairs of women who watch each other: two יבמות, two צרות, a woman and her mother-in-law, a woman and her husband's daughter, and a woman with a girl old enough to understand but too young to take part.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A man may be alone with two יבמות, with two צרות, with a woman and her mother-in-law, with a woman and her husband's daughter, and with a woman and a young girl who understands what relations are but does not yet give herself to them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new ruling: cases where יחוד is allowed because a second woman is there who will not keep quiet about a sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each pair, the women usually do not get along, or the girl is old enough to tell what she saw. Each woman worries the other will tell, so both stay careful. The second woman's presence therefore works as a guard.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying that being alone with two ordinary women is allowed. The היתר works only because these pairs watch each other closely.

phrases.english: Rava said:
A man may be alone with two sisters-in-law
and with two rival wives,
with a woman and her mother-in-law,
with a woman and her husband's daughter,
with a woman and a young girl
who knows the meaning of relations,
but does not give herself over to relations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִתְיַיחֵד אָדָם עִם שְׁתֵּי יְבָמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the איסור to cases where יחוד is allowed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יחוד is allowed with pairs of women who will watch and report on each other.

steps.title: At what age are children called grown up?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about grown children sleeping in separate garments and asks what age counts as grown.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: once they have grown, each one sleeps in his or her own garment. How old is that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and asks how old a child must be to count as grown. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows a parent to share a bed with young children, but once they grow, each must be covered separately. The משנה never gave an age, so the גמרא asks for one.

phrases.english: When they have grown up, this one sleeps in his garment, etc.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה about a parent sharing a bed with his children.

phrases.english: And how much?
phrases.notes: He means: how old must they be?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה after the discussion of being alone with women.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The age at which a child counts as grown for this rule.

steps.title: First answer: a girl at nine, a boy at twelve
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי says a girl counts as grown at nine years and one day, and a boy at twelve years and one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר רב עוא said in the name of רב אסי: a girl at nine years and one day, a boy at twelve years and one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer: the ages are nine for a girl and twelve for a boy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A girl reaches the cutoff earlier than a boy. After these ages a parent may no longer share one covering with the child.

keyTerms.meaning: and one day (just past the birthday)

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Rav Avva said
phrases.notes: Some versions have the name in round brackets and some have the one in square brackets. It is the same person.

phrases.english: Rav Asi said:

phrases.aramaic: תִּינוֹקֶת בַּת תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד,
phrases.english: A girl at nine years and one day,

phrases.aramaic: תִּינוֹק בֶּן שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד.
phrases.english: a boy at twelve years and one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר רַב עַוָּא אָמַר רַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Girl: nine years and one day; boy: twelve years and one day.

steps.title: Second version: a girl at twelve, a boy at thirteen
steps.stepSummary: Others report the ages as twelve for a girl and thirteen for a boy. Both versions agree that the real sign is the start of physical maturity.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: a girl at twelve years and one day, a boy at thirteen years and one day. In both versions, it depends on the signs of maturity described in the פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report with higher ages. It then says both versions measure the same thing: the start of physical maturity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two versions disagree about the numbers but agree on the reason. The cutoff is when the body starts to mature, as the פסוק in יחזקאל describes.

keyTerms.meaning: and this one and that one (both versions)
the breasts were formed (a sign of maturity)

phrases.english: There are those who say:

phrases.aramaic: תִּינוֹקֶת בַּת שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד,
phrases.english: A girl at twelve years and one day,

phrases.aramaic: תִּינוֹק בֶּן שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה וְיוֹם אֶחָד,
phrases.english: a boy at thirteen and one day,
and in both versions, it is the point where there are
"Your breasts were formed and your hair grew."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 16:7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the answer in step 23 and states what both versions share.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Girl: twelve years and one day; boy: thirteen years and one day. Both versions depend on the onset of maturity.
steps.whatToRemember: Whichever version of the ages you follow, the real point is the start of physical maturity.

steps.title: If she is embarrassed, it is forbidden at any age
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the permission applies only while the girl is not embarrassed to stand undressed before her father. Once she is embarrassed, it is forbidden, because her desires have begun.
steps.simpleTranslation: רפרם בר פפא said in the name of רב חסדא: this was taught only when she is not embarrassed to stand undressed before him. If she is embarrassed, it is forbidden. Why? Because desire has taken hold of her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא adds a limit to the permission. A girl's own embarrassment ends it, even before the ages just given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ages are not the only test. If the girl already feels shame about being undressed, her desires have started, and the father may no longer sleep close to her.

keyTerms.meaning: has clothed her (taken hold of her)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rafram bar Pappa said that Rav Chisda said:
They taught this only when she is not embarrassed
to stand undressed before him,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בּוֹשָׁה לַעֲמוֹד לְפָנָיו עֲרוּמָּה – אָסוּר.
phrases.english: but if she is embarrassed to stand undressed before him, it is forbidden.
What is the reason? Desire has taken hold of her.
phrases.notes: Literally, "desire has clothed her." Her feeling of shame shows that her desires have begun.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the age rule from steps 23–24 with a test based on the girl's own feelings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once a girl is embarrassed to stand undressed before her father, sleeping close to her is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the rule follows the girl's actual maturity, not just a number.

steps.title: רב חסדא questions holding a granddaughter on the lap
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר אבא visits his son-in-law רב חסדא and puts his granddaughter on his lap. רב חסדא asks whether he isn't worried that she might be betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר אבא came to the house of his son-in-law רב חסדא. He took his daughter's daughter and sat her on his lap. רב חסדא said to him: Doesn't the master think she might be betrothed?
steps.whatsHappening: A story begins. רב חסדא challenges his father-in-law for holding a girl who might already be betrothed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the girl were betrothed, she would count as a married-designated woman, and holding her close would be improper. רב חסדא is questioning whether this closeness is allowed.

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Abba came
to the house of Rav Chisda, his son-in-law.
He took his daughter's daughter
and sat her on his lap.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר דְּמִקַּדְּשָׁא?
phrases.english: He said to him: Doesn't the master think that she is betrothed?
phrases.notes: רב חסדא, the girl's father, is the one asking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about closeness with a young girl in the family.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר אבא's act of sitting his granddaughter on his lap.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: She might be betrothed, so holding her close would not be appropriate.

steps.title: רב אחא: you would not betroth a minor against רב's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא answers that if she were betrothed, רב חסדא would have broken רב's ruling that a father should not betroth his daughter while she is a minor.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Then you have gone against רב. רב יהודה said in the name of רב, and some say it was רבי אלעזר: a man may not betroth his daughter while she is a minor. He must wait until she grows up and says, "I want so-and-so."
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא pushes back: she can't be betrothed, because that would mean you broke רב's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב forbids betrothing a daughter before she is old enough to choose. Since רב חסדא surely follows this, the girl is not betrothed, so there is no problem.

phrases.english: He said to him: You have gone against Rav.
As Rav Yehuda said that Rav said,
and some say it was Rabbi Elazar:
It is forbidden for a man to betroth his daughter
while she is a minor,
until she grows up and says: "I want so-and-so."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Removes the worry by appealing to a known ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The girl might be betrothed, so holding her is improper.
steps.terutzMaskana: Following רב, a father does not betroth a minor daughter, so she is not betrothed.
steps.whyThisMatters: It records רב's well-known rule that a daughter should not be betrothed until she can choose for herself.

steps.title: רב חסדא: you went against שמואל's rule about using a woman
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers back that his father-in-law broke שמואל's rule that one may not make use of a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: The master has also gone against שמואל, since שמואל said: one may not make use of a woman!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא turns the challenge around. Holding the girl goes against a ruling of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if she is not betrothed, שמואל forbids any personal use of, or closeness with, a woman. רב חסדא argues that holding the girl on his lap falls under this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: one may not make use of a woman

phrases.english: The master too has gone against Shmuel,
phrases.notes: The גמרא doesn't say who is speaking, but this is רב חסדא answering back.

phrases.english: as Shmuel said: One may not make use of a woman!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A counter-challenge after רב אחא's answer in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא's act of holding the girl on his lap.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל forbids making any use of a woman, and holding her close seems to be included.

steps.title: רב אחא starts to answer with another ruling of שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא says he follows a different statement of שמואל and starts to quote it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I hold like the other statement of שמואל, as שמואל said:
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא begins his defense by pointing to a different ruling of שמואל. This line sets up the quote that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of rejecting שמואל, רב אחא says שמואל himself said something else that permits what he did. The actual statement continues past this point.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא כְּאִידַּךְ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל סְבִירָא לִי,
phrases.english: He said to him: I hold like the other statement of Shmuel,
as Shmuel said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the challenge in step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Appeals to another statement of the same authority
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's rule forbids holding the girl.
steps.terutzMaskana: A different statement of שמואל, quoted next, allows it.
